claims.text: A module is a set of .tf files kept together in one folder; every configuration is a (root) module, a folder called from another configuration with a module block is a child module, and nothing inside the folder marks it as a module.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Modules (overview: a module is a container for .tf files in a directory; root and child modules); Language > Modules > Module Blocks

claims.text: In a module block, a local source path must start with ./ or ../ (here ../../modules/kind-cluster, which from deploy/tofu/lessons/moved-into-module reaches deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster); most other arguments set the module's input variables by name.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Modules > Module Sources (Local Paths); Language > Modules > Module Blocks (Module Inputs)

claims.text: An input variable is declared with a variable block; one with no default must be set by the caller (it is required), while one with a default may be left out. Inside the module it is referenced as var.<name>.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Variables and Outputs > Input Variables (Declaring, default, Using Input Variable Values: var.<NAME>)

claims.text: An output value is declared with an output block and its value argument; a calling configuration reads it as module.<MODULE NAME>.<OUTPUT NAME>.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Variables and Outputs > Output Values (Accessing Child Module Outputs)

claims.text: Resources in a child module are encapsulated: the calling configuration cannot reference their attributes directly, only the module's output values; a reference to a name the module does not declare as an output is an error that tofu validate reports.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Modules > Module Blocks (Accessing Module Output Values: resources are encapsulated); Language > Values > Outputs; CLI > tofu validate

claims.text: The kind_cluster resource of tehcyx/kind 0.11.0 exports endpoint, cluster_ca_certificate, client_certificate and client_key attributes; kind-cluster's outputs.tf describes endpoint as the address of the cluster's API server.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt (apply completes); examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/outputs.tf at stage-3 (description of output endpoint)

claims.text: kind-cluster's outputs.tf at stage-3 declares outputs endpoint, cluster_ca_certificate, client_certificate and client_key; only client_key has sensitive = true.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/outputs.tf at stage-3 lines 5-21

claims.text: kind-cluster's variables.tf at stage-3 declares name (string, no default), workers (number, default 0) and published_ports (default []); the moved-into-module call gives only name and workers; the node image is not a variable.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/variables.tf at stage-3 lines 4-24; modules/kind-cluster/main.tf line 16

claims.text: A kindest/node image tag names the Kubernetes version the node runs: kindest/node:v1.34.11 runs Kubernetes v1.34.11, so every cluster made by kind-cluster runs the same Kubernetes version.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start > Creating a Cluster (--image, node images per Kubernetes version); kind v0.33.0 release notes (image list)

claims.text: A module declares the providers it uses in its own terraform { required_providers } block; kind-cluster declares tehcyx/kind version 0.11.0 there.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Providers > Provider Requirements (each module must declare its own provider requirements); kind-cluster/main.tf lines 5-12 at stage-3

claims.text: Further down kind-cluster's main.tf, a dynamic "node" block with for_each = range(var.workers) adds one worker node block per worker; with workers = 0 none is added.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/main.tf at stage-3 lines 38-43

claims.text: required_version in the terraform block constrains which OpenTofu versions may run the configuration (here ~> 1.10.0).
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Settings (Specifying a Required OpenTofu Version)

claims.text: A resource declared in a child module has an address prefixed by module.<call name>., e.g. module.cluster.kind_cluster.this; plans and tofu state list show that address.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > State > Resource Addressing (module path); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt (state list line)

claims.text: Without the moved block, with first-cluster's state in moved-into-module, the plan prints 'kind_cluster.this will be destroyed', 'module.cluster.kind_cluster.this will be created' and 'Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.'
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt lines 1-5 (real run)

claims.text: A moved block with from (old address) and to (new address) makes OpenTofu treat the object recorded at the old address as now at the new one; the plan prints 'has moved to' and, here, 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.'
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Modules > Refactoring (moved block); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt lines 7-9

claims.text: After tofu apply with the moved block, tofu state list in moved-into-module prints module.cluster.kind_cluster.this, and the apply reports 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt (apply and state list lines)

claims.text: tofu-moved.sh, run after tofu-state.sh, moves first-cluster's terraform.tfstate into moved-into-module, plans with the moved block cut out by perl and restored, plans again, applies with -auto-approve and runs tofu state list.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/devops/tofu-moved.sh at stage-3 (header line 3; lines 8-12, 16-32)

claims.text: Destroying and recreating the kind cluster deletes everything that ran in it, because the new cluster starts with new nodes.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start > Deleting a Cluster; devops.l3.plan-and-apply (replacement loses what runs in the cluster)

claims.text: Make a setting a module variable when callers truly need to differ in it; each setting left out is held the same for every caller (opposing view: when one environment must try a change first, that setting must be a variable).
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Modules > Develop > When to write a module; examples/don-hang kind-cluster/main.tf header comment

claims.text: kind get clusters prints the names of existing kind clusters; after tofu-moved.sh it still lists donhang-iac, since the apply reported 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start (kind get clusters); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-moved.txt (Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.)

claims.text: An output with sensitive = true has its value hidden in plan and apply output, but OpenTofu still records the value in the state, readable in plain text by anyone who can read the state.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Values > Output Values (sensitive: Suppressing Values in CLI Output; sensitive values are still recorded in the state); kind-cluster/outputs.tf header comment at stage-3
